# rolebox
Turn one coding agent into a configured engineering team.

Specialist YAML roles with their own prompts, models, skills and permissions — run as explicit
graph
s, with memory that survives the session.
One plugin for opencode, pi, dsh and Codex.
The role picker, opened from the composer: Filter roles searches the 18 loaded roles, each row a dis
play name and a one-line description, and the header names the current selection, Base agent.

## What it is
A general coding agent is one agent with one prompt. rolebox turns it into *your* configured team: s
pecialists defined in YAML, each with its own prompt, model, skills and permissions, working the sam
e task together. What they learn survives the session — decisions, conventions and lessons persist i
n memory and come back at the next session start.
On DSH, roles can collaborate through persistent peer teams: invite complementary specialists, excha
nge events, claim tasks, and continue work across turns. Team execution on other hosts is deferred.
Structured workflows use **declared** graphs: `graph_declare` names each node's agent, brief, and pe
rmitted outcomes; the host dispatches entry nodes and workers settle them with `graph_submit_outcome
`. Graph nodes advance only through accepted outcomes, with bounded loops and inspectable state.
**At a glance**
- **Roles** — 18 specialists on the public oh-my-role registry, or write your own in one YAML file.
- **Runtime** — the graph v3 outcome protocol: declared nodes and edges, accepted outcomes, bounded

repair loops.
- **Memory** — SQLite + FTS5, auto-injected at session start and searchable from the C

LI.
- **Tools** — 32 `lsp_*` language-server tools, `hashline_*` edits anchored to content hashes, s

kills, references, custom functions and hooks.
- **Desktop** — a 12-tool `computer_*` family: `compu
ter_screenshot`, `computer_windows`, `computer_displays`, `computer_focus`, `computer_click`, `compu
ter_move`, `computer_scroll`, `computer_drag`, `computer_type`, `computer_key`, `computer_status`, `

computer_permissions`.

## See it work
Every screenshot in this README was captured from a live dsh session on a demo workspace. Each capti
on states only what that capture shows.
### 1 · Every loaded role, on one page
Settings → Rolebox: the 18 roles that loaded, each with its slug, description and declared tool poli
tings → Rolebox: the 18 roles that loaded, each with its slug, description and declared tool policy.
Each card carries the display name, the slug at the right (`ai-designer`, `apk-reverse-engineer`, `c
omment-writer` in the capture), a description paragraph, then three label/value rows — **Model**, **
Mode**, **Max steps** — and a `Tool policy:` footer. In this capture every visible card reads Model
`default`, Mode `primary`, Max steps `not set` and `Tool policy: none declared`; **no card names a s
ource or origin path**. The header carries the `18 roles` badge, the `Refresh`, `Reload roles` and `
Open monitor` buttons, and a right-aligned `Loaded 18 roles · <time>` line recording when the load h
itor` buttons, and a right-aligned `Loaded 18 roles · <time>` line recording when the load happened.
### 2 · Work is declared as a graph, not prompted node by node
The TypeScript Engineer loads its own skill, reads the protocol reference, and declares the work wit
ngineer loads its own skill, reads the protocol reference, and declares the work with graph_declare.
The role does not do the work inline. It inspects the repo and records a baseline before editing — t
he sample project’s test command → 4 pass / 0 fail, `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0 — then names one real de
sign point: `Task` has no completion state at all, so `removeCompleted()` needs one. It takes the mi
nimal, backward-compatible reading — an optional `completed?: boolean` on `Task` plus `removeComplet
ed(): number` returning the removed count — and passes that decision to the worker explicitly.
It then declares `graph_declare · taskstore-remove-completed` and yields the turn so the engine can
schedule it. The plan names exactly two nodes and one bounded repair round:
- **`change`** (`change-applier`) — implement `removeCompleted(): number` in `src/store.ts`, add the
optional `completed?: boolean` field to `Task` in `src/task.ts`, add a focused test in `tests/task.

test.ts`, and run the sample project’s test command and `tsc --noEmit`.
- **`review`** (`verificatio
n`, independent) — read the actual files and re-run both checks against the same baseline.
The turn closes on the declaration being started (`start.kind: started`, phase `executing`, node `ch
ange` dispatched). The capture states no execution budget.
### 3 · Independent verification, then reconciliation
Accepted results come back; the parent reconciles them, re-runs the checks itself, and states what w
as verified and what remains uncertain.

## What you get
| | Default single agent | With rolebox |
| **Who does the work** | One prompt for every task | Specialists with their own prompt, model, skil

ls and permissions |
| **Remembering** | Sessions start blank | SQLite + FTS5 memory, auto-injected

at session start |
| **Switching** | Reconfigure and restart | Switch role in place; the transcript

survives |
| **Concurrency** | One agent at a time | Parallel dispatched workers with engine-managed

limits |
| **Autonomy** | Free-form chat | Declared graphs with accepted outcomes and bounded repai

r loops |
| **Code navigation** | Text search | 32 `lsp_*` tools — definition, references, rename, d

iagnostics, call hierarchy |
| **Editing** | Line numbers that drift | `hashline_*` edits anchored t

o `LINE#HASH` content hashes |
| **Observability** | Whatever the host logs | Monitor pane, `rolebox

monitor` TUI, channel-filtered logs |
| **Desktop** | None | 12-tool computer-use family: screensho

t, windows, displays, focus, click, move, scroll, drag, type, key, status, permissions |

ng** | Restart to pick up changes | Edit YAML, hot-reload the asset |
